config._note: HR/labour approval record (urenstaat). A single Timesheet captures the hours an employee logged for one period plus a submit -> approve/reject -> reopen approval workflow (x-openregister-lifecycle on `status`). ADR-062 round-2 rework: (1) total-hours KPI stat top-left so the approver sees the claimed volume at a glance; (2) the data widget SPLIT into 'Time entry' (period/description/project/cost centre/billable -- what was worked) and 'Approval' (status/submittedAt/approvedBy/approvedAt/rejectionReason -- the workflow trail), each excluding employeeId since the Related panel already resolves and links the claiming Employee by name; (3) related alongside both, matching their combined height. Files sits full-width below for approval evidence and signed timesheets (approval documents matter, so they are on the body, not a tab). NO email/calendar/talk widgets -- the Timesheet schema declares no comms linkedTypes and a labour record does not correspond; any communication is with the person (Employee), not the record. lifecycleActions expose the schema's own submit/approve/reject/reopen transitions (guarded server-side by NoSelfApprovalGuard). Audit history is pushed to a sidebar tab as a rarely-scanned surface.

config._note: Expense-reimbursement claim (onkostendeclaratie). A single Expense holds one claim (amount / currency / category / date + attached receipt) and a submit -> approve/reject -> reimburse lifecycle (x-openregister-lifecycle on `status`). Content starts at gridY 0 with the 'Claim' data (title/description/amount/currency/category/expenseDate/receiptFile) then 'Approval' (status/submittedAt/approvedBy/approvedAt/rejectionReason/reimbursedAt) below it, both excluding employeeId since Related already resolves the claiming Employee by name; an amount KPI stat sits top-right so the payout figure is unmissable, with Related beneath it matching the combined left-column height. The Files widget (receipt / bon) runs full-width AFTER the domain cards, same placement convention as Timesheet's approval evidence -- the approver reads the claim record first, then opens the receipt to verify it. NO email/calendar/talk -- Expense declares no comms linkedTypes; a reimbursement claim is a financial/HR record, not a correspondence thread. lifecycleActions expose submit/approve/reject/reimburse (approve/reject guarded server-side by NoSelfApprovalGuard; reimburse is terminal). Audit history is a sidebar tab.

Hub archetype: Employee is the record every other HR/payroll schema in hrmq points AT (EmploymentContract.employeeId, Payslip.employeeId, Timesheet.employeeId, Expense.employeeId — all now canonical $ref relations, ADR-062 rule 7), so the page's job is to be the single place an HR/payroll admin lands to see one person's whole labour and pay picture. ADR-062 round-2 rework: the data widget is SPLIT into 'Person' (employeeNumber/firstName/lastName/dateOfBirth/bsn — the identity attributes) at 8-wide beside an in-grid stats-block (KPIs, top-right — replaces the deprecated summaryAggregates header chips) at 4-wide; 'Employment & compliance' (startDate/endDate/grossMonthlySalary/taxTableColor/ID-document retention/30%-ruling/A1 posting/jurisdiction-specific onboarding flags — 18 fields, genuinely this schema's bulk) runs full-width below since it has no natural width-4 partner. Contracts and Timesheets are paired FK-scoped lists, then Payslips (allowCreate:false — payroll-generated, not hand-created from here) and Expenses, then org-chart-basic (2026-07-13) adds an Assignments FK-scoped list (OrgAssignment.employeeId — the placements this employee holds across the org hierarchy) as a full-width row, and performance-reviews-mvp (2026-07-13) adds a Beoordelingen FK-scoped list (PerformanceReview.employeeId — the ADR-001 Rule 6 dossier anchoring: performance data lives on the personnel dossier, not a separate module) as a further full-width row, before the personnel-file Files leaf, which shifts down. Files is justified by identityDocumentVerified/identityDocumentRetainedUntil/loonheffingenVerklaringOnFile — real statutory document-retention fields on this schema, not a generic add. NO calendar/contacts/talk: Employee declares no appointment or comms linkedType — the person's own identity data lives on this record, it is not a link to a separate NC contact. No lifecycleActions — Employee carries no x-openregister-lifecycle. Audit history stays a sidebar tab.

config._note: Leaf compliance record: no other schema in hrmq references EmploymentContract by FK, so the page is a simple two-panel layout -- the data widget (type/writtenContract/dates/hoursPerWeek/hourlyWage/cao/caoSchaal/awfTariff plus the jurisdiction-specific fields: workingTimeDocumented, overtimeMultiplier, ftePartOfYearMinijob, dpaeFiledBeforeStart) at 8-wide, excluding employeeId since the Related panel already resolves and links the owning Employee by name -- and Related at 4-wide for that one meaningful outbound ref. cao-library (2026-07-14): the ct-data widget excludes only employeeId, so the contract's cao (the referenced CAO library id) and caoSchaal (its pay scale) render here for free -- no widget change needed. No child lists (nothing points at a contract), no files/calendar/comms leaves (no linkedType or document field evidence on this schema), no lifecycleActions (EmploymentContract has no x-openregister-lifecycle). Audit history is a sidebar tab.

config.description: Gegenereerde HR-documenten (arbeidsovereenkomst, aanbiedingsbrief, werkgeversverklaring, getuigschrift) via docudesk.

config._note: hrmq-docudesk-documents (2026-07-13): GeneratedDocument is hrmq's log of ONE docudesk render+store handoff (design.md D1), the PayrollGLPostDetail split applied to a document instead of a ledger entry -- gd-status leads with the outcome facts (status/generatedAt/errorMessage), gd-related resolves the Employee and (nullable) EmploymentContract, gd-data carries the remaining fields (documentType/templateRef/filePath) below. No lifecycleActions -- HrDocumentService drives every transition server-side, exactly the PayrollGLPostDetail precedent. Unlike every other hrmq detail page this one IS a document, so the sidebar keeps the library's default Files tab (the stored PDF -- design.md D4, 'the whole point') alongside the default Audit Trail tab, hiding only Notes/Tags/Tasks which carry no meaning here: the custom audit-only `tabs` override the rest of hrmq uses would suppress Files too (CnObjectSidebar's open-enum `tabs` widget registry has no `files` entry), so this page opts into `hiddenTabs` instead of `tabs` -- a deliberate, documented deviation from the fleet's usual sidebar convention, needed to actually show the per-object file. payslip-pdf-docudesk (2026-07-14): gd-data additionally excludes the new payslipId/jaaropgaafId $ref fields -- gd-related resolves both.

config._note: Financial-document archetype (x-schema-org: schema:Invoice), same family as Expense's amount-first design: three headline tiles (gross pay, net pay, Related-to-Employee) lead the page since that is what an employee or approver checks first, followed by the dense data widget carrying the full gross-to-net withholding breakdown (NL loonheffing/zvw/wkr, DE Lohnsteuer/Soli/Kirchensteuer, FR cotisations/PAS, US FICA/Medicare -- the schema is genuinely multi-jurisdiction: only one jurisdiction's fields populate per real record, but which one varies per payslip so a static manifest cannot cherry-pick per-instance; all fields surface via one widget, sized to its true field count and set to 4 columns full-width rather than clipped at 2). ADR-062 round-2: data widget now excludes employeeId (resolved via Related instead of raw uuid) and the height budget was corrected from the round-1 h7 (which clipped ~54 fields behind a scrollbar) to match content. Stat format uses 'number' not 'currency' because Payslip.currency varies per record (EUR/USD) and a widget's format is static. No files/calendar/comms leaves: nothing in the schema models an attachable payslip document or appointment, and Payslip carries no x-openregister-lifecycle so there are no lifecycleActions. Audit history is a sidebar tab. payslip-pdf-docudesk (2026-07-14): page-level action "Genereer PDF" mirrors EmploymentContractDetail's "Genereer arbeidsovereenkomst" shape -- POST /api/documents/generate with {payslipId: @objectId, documentType: loonstrook}, guarded server-side by DocumentController::authorizePayslip().

config._note: payslip-pdf-docudesk (2026-07-14): the EmploymentContractDetail two-panel shape -- a leaf aggregate record with exactly one meaningful outbound ref (Employee), so jg-data (totals/payPeriodCount/verrekendeArbeidskorting/loonheffingennummer/aggregatedAt, excluding employeeId) sits at 8-wide and jg-related resolves+links the Employee at 4-wide. No lifecycleActions: Jaaropgaaf carries no x-openregister-lifecycle -- it is a pure data aggregate upserted server-side by HrDocumentService (design.md D2/D4), not a workflow. No files widget: the rendered PDF lives on the GeneratedDocument record that references this aggregate via jaaropgaafId (Related on GeneratedDocumentDetail resolves it), not here -- adding a files widget here would fabricate a second copy of the same document relationship. No child lists: nothing else in the schema references Jaaropgaaf by FK besides GeneratedDocument, which is reachable from the Documenten index instead. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

config._note: Batch/reconciliation archetype: a PayrollRun is a per-period aggregate of an administration's payslips, so its page leads with the GL-reconciliation totals (totalGross/totalNet/withholdingLiabilityBalance -- exactly the numbers xc-payroll-gl-reconciliation and xc-withholding-liability-clearing check) as stat KPIs, then the full record (period/administrationId/jurisdiction/status/glLiabilityPosted/glExpensePosted/withholdingsClearedToZero plus the engine stamps engineVersion/calculatedAt) in the data widget below. payroll-core-engine (2026-07-14): Payslip NOW carries a real payrollRunId $ref back to PayrollRun (added by payroll-core-schema), so the page gains the FK-scoped Payslips child list (allowCreate:false -- generation via the engine is the only create path, design.md D5) and the page-level api-call action "(Her)berekenen" (POST /api/payroll/calculate with {runId: @objectId}, guarded server-side by PayrollController::authorizeRun(), draft-only -- non-draft runs get a 400). Still NO lifecycleActions: `status` is a plain enum (draft/approved/posted/paid) with no `x-openregister-lifecycle` transition map on this schema -- driving lifecycleActions here would invent transition names the backend does not guard; the recalculate action is a page action, not a transition. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

config._note: retro-adjustments (2026-07-15): a PayrollAdjustment is a DELTA against a sealed original -- pa-delta leads top-left as the stat KPI an accountant reviews (the net nabetaling/terugvordering amount actually settling into the current run), pa-related sits top-right to resolve the four $ref fields (employeeId, originalPayrollRunId, originalPayslipId, settlementPayrollRunId) at matching height, and pa-data runs full-width below with the remaining record fields (excluding those four $refs, already resolved by Related). No lifecycleActions: status is a plain draft/applied enum with no x-openregister-lifecycle map (the PayrollRunDetail precedent -- design.md D8); the page-level 'Herrekenen' api-call is the only action, guarded server-side by PayrollController::adjust() (404 unresolvable/unauthorized, 400 already-applied). Audit history is a sidebar tab.

config.description: Wage-tax / social-security filings by period and statutory deadline.

config._note: Statutory-deadline archetype: a filing's whole purpose is 'was it filed on time and is proof retained'. loonaangifte-filing-lifecycle (2026-07-12) gave NL filings a real create->review->confirm->send workflow, so the page now leads with a compact status/tijdvakcode/deadline/response widget (fi-status) before the full filing data widget, and exposes the klaarzetten/bevestigen/verzenden/heropenen/corrigeren transitions via lifecycleActions (Timesheet pattern). No stats-block KPI tile is used for Status/Deadline: the vendored app-manifest-v2 schema's stat/stats-block `metric` only supports count/sum aggregation, which cannot echo a non-numeric field (enum/date) of the current object, so fi-status is a `data` widget instead -- schema-valid and functionally equivalent (prominent, top-of-page). No related panel (the schema carries no employeeId/administrationId or any other object-FK -- a filing is an organisation-level record, not scoped to a person). Files is included full-width for the filed submission/deposit proof, justified by the schema's own retainedUntil/furnishedToRecipientDate/filedWithAuthorityDate retention-evidence fields (NL 7yr / DE 6yr / US 4yr retention obligations). No calendar/comms leaves -- deadline is a plain date field, not an appointment/event linkedType. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

config.description: UPA (Uniforme Pensioenaangifte) deliveries by period and sector fund, gated on the referenced payroll run's approval.

config._note: pension-filing-upa-mvp (2026-07-12): same statutory-filing shape as LoonaangifteFilingDetail (create->review->confirm->send, gated on an external precondition), but this schema ALSO carries a real FK (payrollRunId -> PayrollRun, the run the delivery reports on), so the layout follows the TimesheetDetail split instead: pf-status leads top-left with the prominent status/deadline/response facts, pf-related sits top-right at matching height to resolve and link the referenced PayrollRun, then pf-data runs below with the remaining record fields (period/fund/aanleverkenmerk/verzondenDoor), excluding payrollRunId since Related already resolves it. Same reasoning as loonaangifte for NOT using a stats-block: the vendored app-manifest-v2 schema's stat/stats-block `metric` only supports count/sum aggregation over a collection, which cannot echo a non-numeric field (enum/date) of the current object, so pf-status is a `data` widget instead -- schema-valid and functionally equivalent (prominent, top-of-page). No Files leaf: unlike LoonaangifteFiling, PensionFiling carries no retention/proof-of-filing fields (no retainedUntil/furnishedToRecipientDate equivalent) -- the response is captured in-record (responseStatus/responseMessage), not as an attached document. No calendar/comms leaves -- deadline is a plain date field, not an appointment/event linkedType. lifecycleActions expose controleren/bevestigen/verzenden/heropenen/corrigeren, controleren guarded server-side by PayrollRunApprovedGuard. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

config.description: Run-to-run loonmutatie-rapporten: per periode wie is ingestroomd/uitgestroomd en de totale loonkostenverandering (payroll-mutation-reports). Admin/HR only -- gegenereerd via de "Mutatieoverzicht"-actie op een loonrun of via occ hrmq:payroll:mutations --persist.

config._note: payroll-mutation-reports (2026-07-14): a PayrollMutationReport is a PURE, read-only diff snapshot -- never recomputed, never written outside PayrollMutationService (design.md D3) -- so the page leads with the accountant's headline (totalWageCostDelta) plus the entered/left/changed counts as stat KPIs (the PayrollRunDetail stat-tile precedent), then the full record (header fromRunId/toRunId/fromPeriod/toPeriod/administrationId/generatedAt, the four component deltas, the four counts, and the embedded per-employee `lines` array) in the pmr-data widget below -- the PayrollGLPostDetail precedent for an embedded array snapshot rendered inside a plain data widget (its own `lines` field, same shape: a system-generated audit-style record, not user-editable). No lifecycleActions: the schema carries no x-openregister-lifecycle -- a report is either regenerated (superseding this one in place, design.md D7) or not; there is no user-facing status transition to guard. No Files/calendar/comms leaves -- not a document or event. Admin/HR only, mirroring the Payroll nav group.

config.description: Payroll-to-GL posting attempts: one balanced loonjournaalpost handed off to shillinq per approved loonrun.

config._note: payroll-glpost-shillinq (2026-07-12): a PayrollGLPost is hrmq's log of ONE handoff attempt into shillinq's JournalEntry register -- never the journal itself (design.md D1). TimesheetDetail/PensionFilingDetail split: pg-status leads top-left with the prominent outcome facts (status/postedAt/errorMessage), pg-related sits top-right to resolve and link the referenced PayrollRun (a real $ref, unlike journalEntryId), then pg-data runs below with the remaining record fields including the journalNumber/journalEntryId pointer into shillinq (plain display only -- no cross-app deep link in MVP, per design.md's 'posted != materialised' risk note) and the lines snapshot. NO lifecycleActions: status has no x-openregister-lifecycle transition map -- PayrollGLPostService drives every transition server-side from `occ hrmq:glpost:run`, exactly the PayrollRunDetail precedent (never invent a user-facing transition the backend does not guard). No Files/calendar/comms leaves -- this is a system-generated audit record, not a document or event. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

config.description: Netto-loon betaalbatches: per betaalbare loonrun een concept SEPA PaymentRun klaargezet in shillinq.

config._note: payroll-sepa-netpay-shillinq (2026-07-13): a PayrollPaymentBatch is hrmq's log of ONE net-pay handoff attempt into shillinq's PaymentRun register -- never the payment batch itself (design.md D1), same PayrollGLPostDetail shape. pb-status leads top-left with the prominent outcome facts (status/createdAt/errorMessage), pb-related sits top-right to resolve and link the referenced PayrollRun (a real $ref, unlike shillinqPaymentRunRef), then pb-data runs below with the remaining record fields including the runNumber/shillinqPaymentRunRef pointer into shillinq (plain display only -- no cross-app deep link in MVP). Copy says 'klaargezet in shillinq', NEVER 'betaald': created != paid, money only moves after shillinq's controller approves and exports (design.md D4). NO lifecycleActions: status has no x-openregister-lifecycle transition map -- PayrollNetPayService drives every transition server-side from `occ hrmq:netpay:run`, exactly the PayrollGLPostDetail precedent (never invent a user-facing transition the backend does not guard). No Files/calendar/comms leaves -- this is a system-generated audit record, not a document or event. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

config._note: leave-verzuim-mvp (2026-07-12): drives the EXISTING LeaveRequest lifecycle from portal-schemas (submit -> approve/reject, guarded server-side by NoSelfApprovalGuard) -- nothing on the schema changes here, only its UI. TimesheetDetail pattern: the data widget is SPLIT into 'Request' (leaveType/startDate/endDate/hours/reason -- what is being requested) and 'Approval' (status/submittedAt/approvedBy/approvedAt/rejectionReason -- the workflow trail), both excluding employeeId since Related already resolves and links the requesting Employee by name. Files sits full-width below for supporting documents (e.g. a bijzonder-verlof invitation). NO stat KPI tile: unlike Timesheet's hours-sum or Expense's amount-sum, a leave request has no single numeric headline worth a dedicated stat (hours is optional and nullable). lifecycleActions expose exactly submit/approve/reject -- no invented cancel/withdraw edge (PayrollRunDetail _note precedent: never claim a transition the backend does not guard). Audit history is a sidebar tab.

config._note: leave-verzuim-mvp (2026-07-12): administrative-only sickness case -- NO medical/diagnosis data exists on this schema or its widgets (REQ-VWP-002). The 'Case' data widget (firstSickDay/recoveredDate/status/wachtdag/loondoorbetalingPercentage) excludes employeeId since Related already resolves and links the sick Employee by name; the 'Poortwachter milestones' widget surfaces all eight Due/Done WVP dates (probleemanalyse/plan van aanpak/UWV 42-wekenmelding/eerstejaarsevaluatie) so the re-integration clock is the page's second headline fact. Files is labeled and described for gespreksverslagen & plan-van-aanpak process documents ONLY -- repeating the no-medical-data warning, matching the schema's own privacy stance. lifecycleActions expose exactly herstellen/heropenen (gemeld<->hersteld) -- no invented edges. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

config._note: time-attendance-mvp (2026-07-13): raw per-day clock record (klokregistratie) -- AttendanceRecord is raw clock data, Timesheet stays the per-period approved-hours record (design D5, no automation between them). The 'Attendance' data widget excludes employeeId since Related already resolves and links the Employee by name. lifecycleActions expose exactly sluiten/heropenen (open<->gesloten, design D4) -- no invented approval edges (approval lives on Timesheet, not here). No files widget -- the schema carries no document/retention field (the EmploymentContractDetail no-fabricated-leaves reasoning). No stat KPI -- a single day's hours is not a headline aggregate (the LeaveRequestDetail precedent). No comms/calendar leaves. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

config._note: onboarding-wizard-mvp (2026-07-13): the 'Case' widget excludes employeeId (Related resolves the hired Employee) and the six checklist gate fields, leaving startDate/proeftijdEndDate/status; the 'Checklist' widget groups exactly the six gate booleans plus widCheckDate and notes -- the SickLeaveCaseDetail grouped-data pattern. lifecycleActions expose exactly the REQ-OBW-002 edges (contract_bevestigen/gegevens_valideren/gereed_melden/starten/afronden/annuleren) -- no invented edges. Checklist gates are audit-enforced (lib/Standards/Checks/NlOnboardingChecks.php), NOT write-time guards: no transition here blocks on an unmet checklist field -- guard wiring for compliance-checked schemas is owned by the active hrmq-rule-compliance-enforcement change (design.md D2). config._note: recruiting-ats-basic (2026-07-13): the 'Vacancy' widget carries every field (title/description/department/status/publishedDate/closingDate). The 'Sollicitaties' related widget resolves the incoming Application.vacancyId references -- the candidate list per vacancy. lifecycleActions expose exactly publiceren/sluiten (design D3) -- no re-open and no publish-from-closed edge; a closed vacancy is re-created, not resurrected. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

config.description: Sollicitatiepipeline (recruiting-ats-basic): nieuw -> screening -> gesprek -> aanbod -> aangenomen/afgewezen. De status-filter is de MVP-pipeline-surface -- elke fase is een filterwaarde; een kanban-board is een nc-vue widget follow-up (design D7).

config._note: recruiting-ats-basic (2026-07-13): candidate PII (candidateName/email/phone/cvFile/motivation) lives DIRECTLY on this Application -- there is deliberately no separate Candidate entity (AVG data-minimisation, design D2): one object = one retention clock = one delete. The 'Application' widget excludes vacancyId (Related resolves the Vacancy) and the three privacy fields (talentPoolOptIn/rejectedDate/retentionExpiryDate), which instead surface on the dedicated 'Privacy & retention' widget so the AVG retention clock is never buried among ordinary fields. lifecycleActions expose exactly screenen/uitnodigen/aanbieden/aannemen/afwijzen (design D3) -- no invented edges; aannemen's onboarding hand-off (creating the Employee from this data) is a MANUAL follow-up action in the MVP, no cross-object write hook fires here. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

config.description: Offboardingcases per vertrekkende medewerker: exit-gesprek, teruggave bedrijfseigendommen, toegangsintrekking en de eindafrekening (verlofsaldo, vakantiegeld, transitievergoeding, getuigschrift), met de laatste werkdag als klok.

config._note: offboarding-wizard-mvp (2026-07-13): the 'Case' widget excludes employeeId (Related resolves the departing Employee), the checklist/eindafrekening fields and notes, leaving reason/status/lastWorkingDay; the 'Checklist' widget groups exitGesprekDone/assetsIngeleverd/toegangIngetrokken; the 'Eindafrekening' widget groups verlofsaldoUitbetaald/vakantiegeldAfgerekend/transitievergoedingBedrag/getuigschriftVerstrekt/notes -- the OnboardingDetail grouped-data pattern. lifecycleActions expose exactly the REQ-OFB-002 edges (afronding_plannen/eindafrekening_gereedmelden/afronden/annuleren) -- no invented edges. Checklist/eindafrekening gates are audit-enforced (lib/Standards/Checks/NlOffboardingChecks.php), NOT write-time guards: no transition here blocks on an unmet gate field -- guard wiring for compliance-checked schemas is owned by the active hrmq-rule-compliance-enforcement change (design.md D2). Audit history is a sidebar tab.

config.description: Organisatiehiërarchie: afdelingen, teams en kostenplaatsen, elk optioneel onder een bovenliggende eenheid.

config._note: org-chart-basic (2026-07-13): hrmq's first organisational-hierarchy schema. The data widget excludes parentUnitId/managerId since Related already resolves and links both by name (the EmployeeDetail exclude convention). Two FK-scoped object-lists cover the hierarchy's two directions: 'Child units' (OrgUnit.parentUnitId = @objectId, the self-referencing tree) and 'Assignments' (OrgAssignment.orgUnitId = @objectId, who is currently/historically placed here). No lifecycleActions: neither OrgUnit nor OrgAssignment carries an x-openregister-lifecycle (design.md D-table) — a plain record toggled active/inactive, not a workflow (PayrollRunDetail 'never invent a transition' precedent). No stat/stats-block KPI: a unit's headline facts (type/costCenter/active) are plain enum/string/boolean fields the stat widget's count/sum metric cannot echo (LoonaangifteFilingDetail/PensionFilingDetail precedent), so they surface in the data widget instead. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

config.description: Effectief-gedateerde plaatsingen van medewerkers in organisatie-eenheden.

config._note: org-chart-basic (2026-07-13): a simple two-panel leaf like EmploymentContractDetail -- the data widget (role/startDate/endDate) excludes employeeId/orgUnitId since Related already resolves and links both the placed Employee and the OrgUnit by name. No child lists (nothing references an OrgAssignment by FK). No lifecycleActions: OrgAssignment carries no x-openregister-lifecycle -- effective-dating lives on startDate/endDate, not a workflow status (design.md D1). No files/calendar/comms leaves -- the schema declares no such linkedType or document field. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

config.description: Bedrijfseigendommen uitgegeven aan werknemers: laptops, telefoons, voertuigen, gereedschap, toegangspassen en kleding, met een bewaakte innamestatus.

config._note: asset-management-mvp (2026-07-13): a company-owned item with a guarded custody lifecycle (beschikbaar -> uitgegeven -> ingenomen -> beschikbaar, or beschikbaar/ingenomen -> afgeschreven, terminal -- the Expense precedent). The data widget shows all fields (no $ref to exclude -- Asset has no outbound relations); lifecycleActions expose exactly the four fragment transitions (uitgeven/innemen/vrijgeven/afschrijven), never invented. An FK-scoped 'Uitgiftes' object-list (AssetAssignment.assetId = @objectId) is the inbound-relation direction (D2) -- who has held this asset, ordered most-recent-first, rowRoute to AssetAssignmentDetail. The Files widget (signed uitgiftebonnen) runs full-width after the domain cards, the ExpenseDetail receipt placement. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

config.description: Effectief-gedateerde uitgiftes van assets aan werknemers.

config._note: asset-management-mvp (2026-07-13): a simple two-panel leaf like OrgAssignmentDetail -- the data widget (uitgifteDatum/innameDatum/uitgifteBonSigned/notes) excludes assetId/employeeId since Related already resolves and links both the issued Asset and the receiving Employee by name. No child lists (nothing references an AssetAssignment by FK). No lifecycleActions: AssetAssignment carries no x-openregister-lifecycle -- effective-dating lives on uitgifteDatum/innameDatum, not a workflow status (design.md D1). Audit history is a sidebar tab.

config.description: Beoordelingscycli (jaargesprekken, beoordelingen, tussentijdse gesprekken) waaronder PerformanceReview-dossiers per medewerker worden verzameld.

config._note: performance-reviews-mvp (2026-07-13): the orchestration half of the performance-review MVP (ADR-001 Rule 6 — sub-pages under the EXISTING Personeel/EmployeesGroup, no new top-level menu). The 'Cycle' data widget carries every field (name/year/type/status/startDate/endDate — no $ref to exclude, ReviewCycle has no outbound relations). The 'Beoordelingen in deze cyclus' object-list (PerformanceReview.cycleId = @objectId) is the cycle's in-progress roster, rowRoute to PerformanceReviewDetail. lifecycleActions expose exactly openen/sluiten (concept->open->gesloten, hr-performance.json) -- no re-open edge, a closed cycle is history (the Vacancy no-resurrection precedent). Audit history is a sidebar tab.

content.emptyText: No reviews in this cycle yet

config._note: performance-reviews-mvp (2026-07-13): the dossier half of the performance-review MVP (ADR-001 Rule 6 — the primary surface is actually the EmployeeDetail emp-reviews row; this page is a routed detail, reached from that row, the cycle's review list, or the deepLink, and is deliberately NOT a menu child, the TimesheetDetail convention). The 'Beoordeling' data widget carries rating/sterktes/ontwikkelpunten/afspraken/goals/besprokenOp/vastgesteldDoor, excluding employeeId/cycleId/reviewerId (Related resolves and links all three by name) and userId (the internal @me self-service field, not a display fact). Goals are recorded INSIDE this review (design D2 — no separate Goal entity anywhere in the register); besprokenOp/vastgesteldDoor are stamped on the carrying writes of bespreken/vaststellen. lifecycleActions expose exactly indienen/bespreken/vaststellen/heropenen (hr-performance.json) -- vaststellen is guarded server-side by the existing NoSelfApprovalGuard (the employee under review may not vaststellen their own beoordeling); heropenen is the correction edge back to besproken. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

pages.title: Simuleer loonstrook
pages._note: proforma-payslip design.md D6: manifest v2 has no declarative primitive for a persist-nothing interactive compute-form. open-form is bound to a register/schema and PERSISTS the created object -- exactly what a pro-forma simulation must not do. api-call only interpolates fixed/@token params against a form-less trigger and surfaces a toast + page refresh -- it cannot gather a bespoke set of hypothetical inputs (bruto, tabel, geboortedatum, deeltijdfactor, bijzondere beloning, periode) nor render the returned JSON breakdown. So this page is a host-app SFC (ProformaPayslip.vue, registered in src/registry.js) that renders the input form and calls POST /api/payroll/proforma directly, showing the full gross-to-net breakdown. No register/schema is referenced and no object is ever created -- the stable, test-covered contract is the endpoint (PayrollController::proforma) + the hrmq:payroll:proforma occ command.
